lines: I am 28. My hair has thinned gradually at the front hairline for two years. My father has similar thinning. I have no scalp itching or flaking.
Have you noticed any increase in hair shedding when you wash or brush your hair recently?
Do you style your hair with heat tools like blow dryers or straighteners on a regular basis?
Have you started or stopped any new medications, supplements, or hormonal treatments in the past year?
Have you noticed any widening of your part or a more visible scalp at the crown of your head?

This pattern is commonly seen as hereditary thinning, often called male or female pattern hair loss, given the gradual front hairline thinning over two years and a matching family history. You reported that your hair has thinned gradually at the front hairline for two years, that your father has similar thinning, and that you have no scalp itching or flaking, which points toward a genetic rather than a scalp-disease cause. Gently massage your scalp for a few minutes daily to encourage blood flow, and use a mild shampoo to keep the area clean without harsh rubbing. Avoid tight hairstyles, harsh chemical treatments, and aggressive brushing that can pull on the thinning front hairline. See a dermatologist if the thinning spreads beyond the front hairline, if you develop patchy bald spots, or if it begins to affect your confidence significantly, so they can confirm the cause and discuss options.
